items.title: How El Niño offers a test of whether the world can adapt to a changing climate
items.summary: El Niño is strengthening in a world that is already hotter, raising the risk of drought, floods and crop losses across some of the world’s most important food-producing regions. But unlike many disasters, this one can be seen coming. UN experts say the months ahead offer countries a chance not only to protect the next harvest and our food security, but to prepare for a more unpredictable climate in the long run.

items.title: High-Level Meeting on Sea-Level Rise (AM & PM) 24 September 2026
items.summary: The General Assembly today will hold a high-level meeting on rising sea levels. Occurring on the margins of its ongoing high-level debate, the meeting aims to address the existential threats posed by this phenomenon. The meeting aims to renew high-level political attention to sea-level rise as a cross-cutting issue that implicates climate action, sustainable development, peace and security, human rights and international cooperation. The aim is to shift the international response to the phenomenon from fragmented initiatives towards sustained, coordinated and adequately financed action.
